title: Nonlinear candidate coverage and visible-prefix selector regret
hypothesis: A legal bank of genuinely different whole-well nonlinear paths can achieve candidate-oracle RMSE below 5, and multi-cut visible-prefix evidence plus calibrated uncertainty can retain enough of that coverage without hidden-label routing.

design.model: fixed nonlinear lattice plus independently screened HMM and DTW branches, followed by split-local multi-cut selectors
legal_inputs: MD X Y Z GR TVT_input
frozen cross-fitted E004 E005 E006 E009 paths/actions
frozen E008 legal features with visible-prefix pseudo-cuts
forbidden_inputs: validation hidden TVT in generation or inference
leaderboard feedback opaque artifacts or post-score mutation
harsher_splits: repeated motifs and no-GR synthetic cases
design.promotion: Bank oracle below 5; legal gain >=0.15 versus E006; >=4/5 maps and >=17/25 cells; tail limits; positive every spatial/typewell group; all controls, reproduction, packaging and parity.
design.deployment: Only after statistical promotion. No submission authorized.
design.full_validation_platform: private Kaggle CPU notebook, internet disabled

conclusion: Implementation and local validation passed. Kaggle input v1 failed before hidden-label scoring because the data signature encoded the physical mount path; no v1 output was accepted. Source commit 49ca399 makes profile paths mount-independent without changing the frozen 773-well signature. Corrected private dataset/notebook v2 is ready; full hidden-label validation remains pending execution and independent output review.
